PROJECT: dc2, the devcircles industry insight report. Live at https://devcircles.apexlinks.org, deployed automatically by Cloudflare Workers Builds on every push to master (wait ~60-90s after a push before checking the live site).

GOAL OF THIS PLAN: turn a directory of 43 product descriptions into a surface that makes an investor want to invest within three seconds of landing. That means: real numbers on every card, honest verification, stage and raising status, a founder's face, one-tap contact, and pages worth sharing. Nothing here is allowed to invent a number.

STACK: SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 (runes only: $props $state $derived $effect $bindable — never `export let`), TypeScript, Tailwind v4, adapter-cloudflare (Workers). Package manager is pnpm, never npm or npx. Node 22 (strips TypeScript types natively, so .ts test files run under `node --test` with no build step and no dependencies).

DATABASE: Qdrant only. One collection, `i`, shared with other projects — never create another collection. Every row this project owns carries `s: 'adca'`. Row types: `t: 'p'` product, `t: 'sec'` sector, and (added by this plan) `t: 'x'` investor interest. Helpers live in src/lib/server/qdrant.ts: `scroll(env, filter, limit)`, `retrieve_one(env, id)`, `upsert(env, points)`, `remove(env, id)`, `uuid_from(string)` (async, SHA-256 of 'adca:' + input), `eq(key, value)`, `f(...conds)`. `upsert` attaches the 4096-dim zero vector under the named vector `i` for you — never pass a vector yourself. Secrets are read with `import { env } from '$env/dynamic/private'` and passed as the first argument to those helpers.

PRODUCT PAYLOAD SCHEMA (single-letter keys, this is deliberate, keep it):
s tenant 'adca' | t type 'p' | g slug | n name | u url | l link label | r status: l live / p preview / u in review | c sector char | cn sector name | o one-liner | w what it does | h why it matters | x where it can grow | d launch date | q users/signups | m revenue y/n/'' | a monthly revenue naira | z team size | k proudest metric | b builder contact object {n name, e public email, p phone, l linkedin, c location} | e PRIVATE ownership email | j created epoch seconds.

NEW KEYS THIS PLAN ADDS (all optional strings, all default to ''):
hm headline metric value | hl headline metric label | hv headline verification: v verified by devcircles / s self-reported | sg stage: i idea / b in beta / l launched / r making revenue / s scaling | ra raising: y / n / '' | rt raise target text | fp founder photo url | ev evidence text or url | vd link last verified, ISO date string | hj epoch seconds when the builder last confirmed their figures.

STALENESS DOCTRINE — the idea the whole surface rests on. Every figure on this site is wrong eventually. A number typed in March is a lie in September, whoever typed it, and no amount of chasing builders fixes that. So this plan does not try to keep data fresh. It makes the age of every fact visible, and makes decay cost the person who could fix it.

Four rules follow from that, and every step obeys them:
1. NO FIGURE IS EVER SHOWN WITHOUT ITS DATE. `2,400 users · as of march 2026` is honest at any age. `2,400 users` becomes false silently. This is the whole fix, and it costs one field.
2. AGE IS A WEIGHT, NOT A FLAG. src/lib/investor.ts multiplies every builder-reported signal by a freshness factor: full weight to 90 days, half to 180, nothing after. A listing that stops being confirmed sinks down the page on its own. Nobody has to police it, and the builder who wants to be near the top has one obvious thing to do.
3. WHAT A MACHINE CAN RE-DERIVE NEVER GOES STALE. That is why `r` (status), `ev` and `vd` come from scripts/probe.mjs and carry full weight forever, while `hm`, `sg`, `ra` and the metrics come from humans and decay. Keep that split — it is the reason the page can be trusted at all.
4. STALE DATA IS DEMOTED, NEVER DELETED OR HIDDEN. A number from last year is still evidence of what existed last year. Show it, dated, in the past tense. Deleting it would destroy the only record; presenting it as current would be a lie.

`hj` is written by the server on save and by the confirm action, never by a form field — a builder must not be able to backdate or post-date their own freshness stamp.

HARD RULES, BREAKING ANY OF THESE FAILS THE STEP:
1. `e` is the private ownership key. It MUST NEVER reach the browser. src/routes/+page.server.ts and src/routes/[slug]/+page.server.ts both `delete p.e` before returning — never remove that, and any new public loader you write must do the same. `b.e` is the separate, deliberately public contact email.
2. All user-facing text is lowercase. Labels, buttons, headings, microcopy, empty states.
3. Tailwind utilities only. No inline `style=` attributes, no `<style>` blocks. Colours come from src/app.css @theme tokens only: text-ink, text-cobalt, bg-cobalt, text-coral, bg-coral, bg-ochre, bg-teal-brand, bg-plum, font-display. Never a raw hex or rgb value. If you need a new colour, add it to @theme in src/app.css first.
4. snake_case for every variable and function name.
5. No comments in code.
6. Any form that a human types into submits on Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, never plain Enter.
7. Never start the dev server. `.log` in the repo root holds output from a dev server the user runs; read it when diagnosing, never launch one.
8. Never put `wrangler types` in the build script.
9. Never edit a test file. Tests are staged under plan/tests/ and copied into place with the exact `cp` command the step gives. plan/verify_tests.sh byte-compares every placed test and runs at the front of every gate.

COMMANDS: `pnpm check` (svelte-check, must stay at 0 errors — 4 pre-existing warnings about `state_referenced_locally` in src/lib/sector_picker.svelte and src/routes/[slug]/edit/+page.svelte are expected and fine). `pnpm test` (node --test, added by the first step). `node scripts/seed.mjs` re-upserts every product from seed.json into Qdrant, preserving builder-owned fields. `.env` in the repo root holds QDRANT_URL and QDRANT_KEY for the scripts.

AFTER EACH STEP: git add . && git commit scoped to that step id, then push. A failed push is fine, the commit is what matters.

probe_cron.s:
Make the machine-checked half of the data refresh itself, so it can never go stale.

This is the point of splitting the schema the way it is split. `r`, `ev` and `vd` are re-derived from the live web, so they are true every month without a single human being chased. Only the figures a person typed decay.

Create .github/workflows/probe.yml with exactly this content:

name: probe

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 1 * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  probe:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - name: write env
        run: |
          echo "QDRANT_URL=${{ secrets.QDRANT_URL }}" > .env
          echo "QDRANT_KEY=${{ secrets.QDRANT_KEY }}" >> .env
      - run: node scripts/probe.mjs
      - run: node scripts/probe_apply.mjs

It runs at 06:00 on the first of every month, and can be triggered by hand from the Actions tab.

The two repository secrets it needs are QDRANT_URL and QDRANT_KEY, which are NOT set yet and cannot be set from inside this repo. After creating the file, print this line for the user and move on — do not block on it, the workflow file is the deliverable:

  needs `gh secret set QDRANT_URL` and `gh secret set QDRANT_KEY` before the first scheduled run.

Do not commit any secret value into the workflow or the repo.
probe_cron.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && test -f .github/workflows/probe.yml && grep -qF "cron: '0 6 1 * *'" .github/workflows/probe.yml && grep -qF 'node scripts/probe_apply.mjs' .github/workflows/probe.yml && ! grep -qiE 'QDRANT_KEY=[A-Za-z0-9]' .github/workflows/probe.yml && pnpm test && pnpm check

milestone_copy.s:
Steer builders toward the one kind of number that never goes stale. `₦1m a month` is true for about a month. `first ₦1m month: august 2026` is true forever, and tells an investor the same thing plus when it happened. A dated milestone is strictly better than a running total for a directory that cannot update itself daily, and the only thing standing between the two is the hint text under the field. FILE: src/routes/[slug]/edit/+page.svelte AND src/routes/submit/+page.svelte In both files, the investor fieldset's `what that number is` label currently ends with its ``. Add a hint span immediately after that input, inside the same label, in both files: milestones age better than totals. "first ₦1m month, august 2026" stays true; "₦1m a month" stops being true the month it changes. And in both files, under the headline-number input, change the existing placeholder from `2,400` to `2,400 · or: first 1,000 paying users`. Also add, directly under the `for investors` heading paragraph in both files:

whatever you put here is stamped with today's date and shown with it. it keeps full weight for three months, half for three more, then stops counting until you confirm it.

Telling builders the rule up front is what makes the rule work. A decay nobody was told about reads as the site being broken; a decay everybody was told about reads as the site being honest, and gives them a reason to come back.

structured_data.s:
Add JSON-LD to every product page so search engines and link unfurlers understand what each page describes.

FILE: src/routes/[slug]/+page.svelte

In the script block add:

	const ld = $derived(
		JSON.stringify({
			'@context': 'https://schema.org',
			'@type': 'SoftwareApplication',
			name: p.n,
			description: p.o,
			url: p.u,
			applicationCategory: p.cn || p.c,
			...(b.n ? { author: { '@type': 'Person', name: b.n } } : {}),
			...(p.d ? { datePublished: p.d } : {})
		})
	);

Inside the existing `<svelte:head>` block, after the last meta tag, add:

	<link rel="canonical" href="https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/{p.g}" />
	{@html `<script type="application/ld+json">${ld}<` + `/script>`}

The split closing tag is required: Svelte's compiler ends the component's own script block at a literal `</script>` inside a template string.

Also strengthen the shared description. The head currently sets `<meta name="description" content={p.o} />`. Leave it, and add beneath the og tags:

	<meta property="og:url" content="https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/{p.g}" />
	<meta property="og:type" content="article" />

ship.s: prove it on the live site

live_check.s:
Push and verify against production. Cloudflare Workers Builds deploys automatically on push to master; give it 90 seconds before checking.

Run, in order:

git add . && git commit -m "investor surface" && git push

Then wait 90 seconds and check the live site. Every one of these must pass:

1. The homepage renders the traction view and both toggles.
2. The homepage exposes no email address anywhere — this is the leak that was fixed before this plan started and the check exists so it never comes back.
3. /raising responds 200.
4. /robots.txt names the sitemap.
5. A product page carries JSON-LD.

If any check fails, that is this step's problem — fix it here, do not mark and move on. If the failure is that the deploy has not landed yet, wait and check again rather than blocking.
live_check.t: curl -s --max-time 25 https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/ | grep -q 'by traction' && ! curl -s --max-time 25 https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/ | grep -qE '[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}' && [ "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 25 https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/raising)" = 200 ] && curl -s --max-time 25 https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/robots.txt | grep -q 'Sitemap:' && curl -s --max-time 25 https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/cashwyre | grep -q 'application/ld+json'
